heard: One tiny moon looks like a jigsaw puzzle glued back together. When Voyager 2 reached Uranus in 1986, scientists expected its moon Miranda to be a boring ice ball. Instead, they found a patchwork, Frankenstein world with a massive V-shaped scar. Miranda's surface features Verona roops, a staggering cliff reaching up to 12 miles deep. That is 12 times deeper than the Grand Canyon, on a world the size of Texas. One leading theory suggests the moon was shattered by impacts multiple times before reassembling into a chaotic pile. Alternatively, extreme tidal heating from Uranus might have churned the moon's icy interior into these bizarre shapes. With only the southern half ever photographed, nobody knows why.
